clue.text: To overcome Labour, Conservative turned blue

indicators.note: turned means the whole assembled string is read backwards
to overcome is pictured as coming over, so the word to wraps around the party's short name

parts.note: Lab is the usual short form of the UK Labour Party

explanation.surface: A political tale: to beat Labour, a Conservative switched sides and went blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcome' wraps one piece round another, making TLABO; with C added, 'turned' reverses the lot. 'blue' looks like the Tory colour but is the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobalt blue is a deep pigment, so the metal's name stands for that shade.

clue.text: City street to shout about

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shout word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: to cheer is to shout encouragement

explanation.surface: In a city a crowd shouts about the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Chester is a cathedral city in Cheshire, in north-west England.

clue.text: 3 sitcom produced by 24

definitions.meaning: a TV comedy set in the city at 3 down, about the Boswell family
what the cook at 24 across makes in the oven

explanation.definitionFit: Bread was a 1980s BBC sitcom set in Liverpool, and loaves are what a baker makes.

clue.text: Royal fund backs rise of corrupt City

indicators.note: backs means comes behind, so the royal fund follows the turned word
in a down entry, a rise is a word read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: corrupt in the sense of wicked gives evil
a pool is a shared fund of money

explanation.surface: A royal fund supports a corrupt city on the up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise of' turns EVIL upwards to LIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool is a port city on the Mersey in north-west England.

clue.text: Reportedly mean birds

indicators.note: reportedly signals that a word heard spoken is being matched to a similar-sounding one

parts.note: mean in the sense of meagre or petty gives paltry

explanation.surface: A rumour that some birds are stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Poultry are domestic fowl such as chickens and ducks, kept for eggs and meat.

clue.text: Sweet prince is promising bachelor no more

indicators.note: no more means the bachelor's letter is gone from the word

parts.note: budding means promising, as in a budding star

explanation.surface: A sweet prince who seemed a promising catch is a bachelor no longer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no more' removes B from BUDDING, leaving UDDING.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain pudding is the general word for a dessert or sweet course.

clue.text: Yummy barman regularly seen in shadow

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every second one

explanation.surface: An attractive bartender is often spotted in the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: The umbra is the darkest part of a shadow, where light is fully blocked.

clue.text: Is using more than one stopwatch cheating?

definitions.text: Is using more than one stopwatch
definitions.meaning: literally doing the timing with a pair of watches
being unfaithful to a partner by seeing someone else as well

explanation.definitionFit: Two-timing is deceiving a partner by having a second lover, and literally timing with two watches.

clue.text: Arabian soldiers first pursue the old

indicators.note: pursue means follow, so the soldiers and first come after the old word

parts.note: ye is an old form of the
men are soldiers, the ranks
I is the Roman numeral one, so first

explanation.surface: Arabian soldiers first chase after the old.
explanation.definitionFit: Yemen is on the Arabian Peninsula, so a native of it is an Arabian.

clue.text: Two ways to describe article or piece

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the ways enclose the article

parts.note: RD is short for road, another way
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson offering two ways to describe an article or a piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to describe' puts AN between the R and D of STRD.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand is a single thread or fibre, a piece of a rope or a story.

clue.text: Weak tea? Never brew Darjeeling to begin with!

indicators.note: to brew is to stir things together, so these letters are mixed up
to begin with points to the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A complaint that tea is weak, with advice never to brew Darjeeling first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brew' shuffles TEA, NEVER and D (Darjeeling's first letter, from 'to begin with').
explanation.definitionFit: Enervated means drained of energy, feeble and lacking vitality.

clue.text: Opportunity follows the debut of Basil Brush

indicators.note: follows places the opportunity word after the debut letter
the debut of a word is its first appearance, so its first letter is taken

parts.note: room, as in room for manoeuvre, means opportunity or scope

explanation.surface: Basil Brush, the fox puppet of British children's TV, gets his first big chance.
explanation.walkthrough: Basil Brush is a puppet fox from British children's television, which makes 'Brush' read as a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A broom is a long-handled sweeping brush.

clue.text: 500 join in tour round royal house

indicators.note: join in tells us the number letter goes into the middle of the other word
round suggests the letters of tour are turned about into a new order

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A tour party of 500 joins a tour around a royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges TOUR to TUOR and 'join in' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the dynasty that ruled England from Henry VII to Elizabeth I.

clue.text: America's main problem? Moving into action

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for America

indicators.note: a problem leaves the letters of main in a muddle, rearranged
moving signals that the letters of into shift into another order

explanation.surface: A question about America's chief difficulty, answered with a call to get things moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' turns MAIN into NIMA and 'Moving' turns INTO into TION.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation is liveliness or activity, the state of being full of life and movement.

clue.text: Ponders complicated answer

indicators.note: complicated means tangled up, so the letters of ponders are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone thinks hard over a difficult reply.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond is to reply, giving a verbal answer to someone.

clue.text: Review of doing 1 + 2 + 3?

definitions.meaning: a judge's final recap of the evidence for a jury
adding numbers together into a total

explanation.definitionFit: A summing-up is a concluding recap, and adding numbers is literally totting them.

clue.text: Cigar ignited over top of light bulb

indicators.note: something ignited is set ablaze and disturbed, so these letters are shuffled
top of picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A cigar is lit from the top of a light bulb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignited' rearranges CIGAR plus L, the first letter of 'light' picked by 'top of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Garlic grows as a bulb made up of cloves.

clue.text: Give back pound from mouldy mulberries

indicators.note: mouldy means rotten and broken down, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the symbol for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Someone wants a pound refunded for berries that have gone mouldy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mouldy' rearranges MULBERRIES once 'from' has taken out L, the pound sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To reimburse is to repay money someone has spent or lost.

clue.text: Beamed Scotty initially a long way down

indicators.note: initially means the word's first letter is used

parts.note: a mile is a long way to go

explanation.surface: Star Trek's Scotty beams someone a long way down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beamed' evokes Scotty beaming people in Star Trek, but here it means grinned.
explanation.definitionFit: To beam is to grin broadly, so beamed is a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Bear up and manage etc, before society notices

indicators.note: before puts the arranged letters ahead of the society letter
in a down entry, up means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a Ted, short for teddy, is a toy bear

indicators.note: to manage is to sort out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A busy instruction: stand up, sort out the extras, then society sits up and notices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TED into DET and 'manage' rearranges ETC into ECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To detect is to discover or perceive something, so it notices.

clue.text: Old Liberals accept national (and English) complaints

indicators.note: and adds a further letter which also goes inside the party's name
to accept is to take in, so the old party's name contains the abbreviation

parts.note: the Whigs were the forerunners of the Liberal Party

explanation.surface: Historic Liberals listen to grievances from a national, and an English one too.
explanation.walkthrough: The Whigs were the British party that became the Liberals; N and E both go into WHIGS, after the I and after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: Whinges are whining grumbles, British slang for petty complaints.

clue.text: Struggle about new maze

parts.note: a war is a struggle or conflict
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone struggles round a new maze.
explanation.definitionFit: A warren is a maze of tunnels dug by rabbits, or any tangle of passages.

clue.text: Scottish minister no longer has temperature, doctor

indicators.note: no longer has means the letter is taken away from the name

parts.note: Nicola Sturgeon was Scotland's First Minister

explanation.surface: A Scottish politician has recovered from a fever, says the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicola Sturgeon was Scotland's First Minister from 2014 to 2023.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a doctor who operates on patients.

clue.text: Chelsea fan also rioting on Tyneside

indicators.note: rioting suggests wild disorder, so the letters of also are rearranged

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE

explanation.surface: A Chelsea football supporter is also out rioting up in Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: A Sloane Ranger is a posh young Londoner from around Sloane Square in Chelsea, not a football fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sloane is a well-off, upper-class young person associated with Chelsea in London.

clue.text: Man stole diamonds in the East Midlands

indicators.note: stole means took away, so the man's name takes in the other word

parts.note: Lester is a man's name
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A jewel thief robs diamonds somewhere in the Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' looks like the crime but signals LESTER taking in ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester is the county town of Leicestershire, a city in the East Midlands of England.

clue.text: Mathematician keeps things working smoothly, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: an oiler lubricates machinery so it runs smoothly

explanation.surface: A mathematician is said to keep things running without friction.
explanation.walkthrough: Euler is pronounced like oiler.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was an 18th-century Swiss mathematician.

clue.text: Cook delivers off-break

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters of break are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler delivers an off-break, a ball spinning from the off side.
explanation.walkthrough: An off-break is a cricket delivery spinning in from the off side; here 'off' is split away as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A baker is someone who bakes bread and cakes, a kind of cook.

clue.text: Rulers engagements attract not a single word of disapproval

indicators.note: not says the disapproving word is left out of the engagements word

parts.note: bookings are engagements, as for a performer
boo is a jeer of disapproval

explanation.surface: Royal appearances attract no boos at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attract' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Kings are monarchs, the male rulers of kingdoms.

clue.text: A dash of orange liqueur or spirit?

indicators.note: a dash of is a small portion, so only part of the run of words is used

explanation.surface: A question about adding a splash of orange liqueur or a spirit to a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' wants to be the drink beside the liqueur; it is a heavenly being.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a spiritual being, a messenger of God.

clue.text: Gap: "Everything Must Go!"

definitions.meaning: a gap or space allowing passage, as in headroom under a bridge
the slogan of a shop's sell-off sale of all its stock

explanation.definitionFit: Clearance is both the room between objects and a sale emptying a shop of stock.

clue.text: Bit of evidence Piers M. shredded for large organisations

indicators.note: bit of picks a small part, the first letter of the word
shredded means torn up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone named Piers M. shreds incriminating evidence on behalf of big companies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shredded' rearranges PIERSM into MPIRES.
explanation.definitionFit: Business empires are big commercial groups controlled by one person or firm.

clue.text: Admiral's sole upset is in the news

indicators.note: is in tells us the rearranged word sits within the other letters

parts.note: news read as plural new, and N stands for new, gives two Ns

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters of sole are rearranged

explanation.surface: An admiral's lonely distress makes the headlines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'news' is read as plural of 'new', and N stands for new, so it gives two Ns; 'upset' rearranges the fodder that sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio Nelson was the British admiral who won at Trafalgar.
